## Goals

- Related note: [Note Title](../../../notes/03-StatTheory/note-name.qmd)
- Check whether the distribution of the sample mean approaches normality (CLT).

## Simulation

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: fig-clt-r
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the sample mean (R)"
set.seed(2026)
xbar <- replicate(5000, mean(rexp(30, rate = 1)))
hist(xbar, breaks = 50, probability = TRUE, main = "", xlab = "sample mean")
curve(dnorm(x, mean = 1, sd = 1 / sqrt(30)), add = TRUE, lwd = 2)
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: fig-clt-py
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the sample mean (Python)"
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

rng = np.random.default_rng(2026)
xbar = rng.exponential(1, size=(5000, 30)).mean(axis=1)
x = np.linspace(xbar.min(), xbar.max(), 200)
plt.hist(xbar, bins=50, density=True)
plt.plot(x, stats.norm.pdf(x, 1, 1 / np.sqrt(30)), lw=2)
plt.xlabel("sample mean")
plt.show()
```

:::
